You have some questions just ask.

Since many don't know the process of this.

First thing is that submarine service in the US Navy is completely volunteer. You can opt out any time (save when you are underway going to have to stick it out). With me I made sure I was going sub fleet when I signed up.

I thought I was being smart planning for the future when I decided I wanted to be a cook. More on that later.

After boot camp which is the same for everyone you will go to either your "A" school which means your technical school. Oddly enough they have one for cooks. Most of it is just learning to do the math for recipe cards which are all in servings of 100.

So yeah doesn't require a goddamn genius to figure it out. WE HAD PEOPLE FAIL. I spent most my time out and off base as it was at Lackland AFB on the Medina side. So yeah I slept most the times I was in class waking up to take the tests.

We had a handful of pratical lessons where we actually cooked. So I was never fucked with by anyone. My peers hated me and always talked shit, but I didn't care.

After that I went to sub school. That I wasn't able to sleep in. Holy fuck so much shit gets pushed on you so fast. Scariest part is how hands on it is. You do advanced fire fighting in a so called simulation that is controlled, but you catch on fire and extinguish fire.

You also do a flooding simulation that will test you and that made a few quit.

Not sure if they do it anymore, but you do an egress as well. 75ft egress from underwater up a tube and well that is something you never forget.

Once you do the personality tests and pass the classes you are sent to fleet.

You do get a bit of a choice. They let you choose 5 places in order where you want to be stationed. Well I went to Bremerton sub base.

Upon getting to your command you are given barracks, and meal card. When you are on shore most departments just require muster at revelie. Then if you have schools or other obligations do that. Sometimes you get stuck with answering the goddamn ships phone.

I did volunteer work for local restaurants or community shit. Worked at McDonald's for a few weeks. Or building playgrounds and homes.

A month before ship comes into port you do refreshing stuff. Some do the requal of ships systems or whatever. As a cook we planned the menu. We plan for 100 days at sea on SSBN subs. Very rare to be out longer than that.

Longest I was out was 97 days. (My first patrol)

You get the ships stores as well. Most was from Sysco so as cooks we all get to go visit the shows with new menu items and try the food. Quite a lot of freedom planning the menu actually as well as ordering.

My first patrol I had to do the math for all the goddamn shit we needed in relation to the menu cards. That took two weeks. I am not kidding when I say we ordered 1234lbs of sugar.

Once the order is completed they deliver it very quickly. It is deliver on base to a warehouse. It is then separated and counted for accuracy. Once that is done you start to load in into what is called modular stores.

On SSBN subs there is a specific place that is allowed for food stores forward of the fan room on forward compartment 2nd level. There are 24 modules that you are allowed. So you have to load all that shit into the fucking thing. It takes some Tetris level shit to do.

Once that is done you have about a week left before the sub is back.

When turn over happens (SSBN subs have blue and gold crews) you take ownership of the designated area and it is up to you to check all functions and sanitary status of that shit.

You get frozen and parishable items first to load. Not much of a freezer or fridge space so things like milk, fresh veggies and fruit don't last long. Then the mods come in and they open the top of the sub for that and take the old ones out and load the new ones into place.

They lock into the floor so they are secure.

Once that is complete you get eggs. Now there is a lot of fucking eggs delivered and they are stored amidships lower level. (Missle compartment lower level) as it is colder there than anywhere else. Also out of the way.

Then you load in TDU weights. (Weights that are placed into waste containers so they sink when jettison overboard).
